gates.note: The report is an artifact. A repository-wide percentage is not a merge or release gate.
Named-machine budgets live in docs/engineering/benchmark-baseline.json. pnpm bench compares a local run to that file. This status file is not a pull-request failure.

Vitest mounts the shell on an in-memory native adapter. That covers convert/save/reopen/export, malformed and oversized open, recovery, close prompts, keyboard file commands, menu/list/focus/live-region checks, and structural visual contracts. Packaged pixels are the separate pixel-baselines gate. Narrator, scaling, and high contrast stay on native-smoke. This is not WebView2 evidence.
pnpm window:measure times a release executable until Open Image is in the WebView2 accessibility tree. It is not a pull-request failure and it is not WebView2 present time.
pnpm pixels:capture writes packaged WebView2 screenshots of the primary states. Structural DOM contracts remain in the browser-adapter suite. Narrator, scaling, and high contrast stay manual.
pnpm webview2:missing refuses to pass on a machine that already has the Evergreen runtime.

pnpm recovery:packaged kills a release executable after a checkpoint and records the restart prompt. It is not a pull-request failure. The recovery directory must start empty because the packaged app does not follow an overridden APPDATA. pnpm recovery:source records that Open Original and Discard Recovery leave a .savage unchanged.
pnpm recovery:source opens a temporary .savage, kills the release executable, and checks Open Original and Discard Recovery. It is not a pull-request failure.
